population.provider: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
population.locator: ISO3_code=FJI; Variant=Medium; Time=2020..2050; TPopulation1July; source values are thousands of people
population.lineage: Exact annual population snapshot already validated for Fiji v2.8.

resident_food.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
resident_food.locator: Area=Fiji; Item=Fish, Seafood; Element=Food supply quantity (kg/capita/yr); Years=2021..2023
resident_food.method: Three-year arithmetic mean of resident food availability. No separate tourism demand is added.
resident_food.quality_note: All three FAOSTAT observations carry flag E (estimated value).

trade.product: UN Comtrade annual HS trade data
trade.locator: period=2025; reporterCode=242 (Fiji); partnerCode=0 (World); flowCode=M for imports and DX for domestic exports; customsCode=C00; motCode=0; HS0301..0309, HS1604 and HS1605; netWgt in kg
trade.method: Four-digit aggregate net weights are used except HS1604 imports, whose aggregate net weight is blank and is reconstructed from available six-digit net weights. The minimum resident-market import proxy is calculated by HS heading as max(total imports minus reported re-exports, zero), then summed. This prevents processing/re-export throughput from displacing Fiji production.
limitations: The HS160431 caviar import has USD 18181.555 of value but no reported weight and is excluded from the mass total.
Trade product weights are treated one-for-one as market-weight fish equivalent; no species, preservation-state or edible-yield conversion is imposed.
Domestic exports use flow DX and therefore exclude separately reported re-exports.

Same-year retained imports are an accounting proxy: re-exports can come from inventories imported in earlier years, so negative code-level differences are floored at zero rather than netted against unrelated fish products.

fisheries_service_calibration.provider: Fiji v2.7 Fisheries source-traceable calibration carried by Fiji v2.8
fisheries_service_calibration.method: 2020 useful-service demands are divided by observed 2020 capture landings, aquaculture harvest and total domestic harvest to create PJ/Mt mass-link coefficients. These are calibration coefficients, not independent 2020 activity requirements in v2.9.

capture_activity_ceiling.locator: Reported 2020-2021 offshore longline catch of 12,661 tonnes plus estimated coastal commercial catch of 11,000 tonnes; retained from the v2.7 evidence ledger.
capture_activity_ceiling.method: The included 23,661 tonne capture boundary is held constant as a conservative full-horizon screening ceiling. It is not presented as a legal quota or a biological stock assessment.

aquaculture_activity_ceiling.provider: Fiji Ministry of Fisheries and Forestry
aquaculture_activity_ceiling.locator: Table 18, Summary of deliverables: December 2024 targets of 300 tonnes tilapia, 15 tonnes giant river prawn and 35 tonnes black tiger shrimp; December 2028 targets of 600, 150 and 700 tonnes, respectively.
aquaculture_activity_ceiling.actuals_locator: National production of 212.83 tonnes tilapia and 4.095 tonnes freshwater prawn, totaling 216.925 tonnes.
aquaculture_activity_ceiling.method: The latest observed total is an upper envelope through 2023. The plan's detailed Table 18 annual deliverables for tilapia, giant river prawn and black tiger shrimp are summed for 2024-2028; the 2028 total is held constant from 2029 through 2050. These are maximum investible programme envelopes, not production demands.

service_calibration_2020.market_output_basis: One tonne of raw domestic fish becomes one tonne of aggregate market-weight fish. Processing losses and product conversion are not represented in the aggregate v2.9 screen.

capture.rule: Hold the included 2020 capture boundary constant from 2020 through 2050.

aquaculture.rule: Use 216.925 tonnes in 2020-2023, the Table 18 programme totals in 2024-2028, then hold the 1,450-tonne 2028 envelope from 2029 through 2050.

model_policy.resident_food_baseline: 2021-2023 mean FAOSTAT fish and seafood food availability per resident
model_policy.import_rule: The 2025 retained-import proxy (max of imports minus reported re-exports at each HS heading) multiplied by each year's population/2025 population is a minimum; additional high-cost imports remain open
model_policy.export_rule: 2025 domestic-export market-weight volume multiplied by each year's population/2025 population is added to final demand
model_policy.import_variable_cost_role: Screening penalty in million USD/Mt, not a border price. The retained-import pilot with VC=1000 found a maximum FSHFOOD balance dual of 111.38863 discounted in 2024, equivalent to 138.737131 undiscounted; VC=200 remains safely above that observed domestic marginal value.
model_policy.accounting_capacity_regularization_role: Numerical tie-breaker in million USD/(Mt/year) for the four one-year accounting capacities; prevents arbitrary 999999 capacity results while having immaterial cost.
model_policy.service_demand_rule: The former fixed SAD values for FSHCAPSERV, FSHAQSERV and FSHPOSTSERV are zero. Fish production now pulls those intermediate services endogenously.
model_policy.capture_limit: FSHCAPHARV annual activity is capped at 0.023661 Mt/year in 2020-2050 using the included 2020 capture boundary. This is a conservative screening ceiling, not a legal quota or biological stock model.
model_policy.aquaculture_limit: FSHAQHARV annual activity is capped by the observed/programme envelope: 0.000216925 Mt/year in 2020-2023, rising through the detailed 2024-2028 Table 18 deliverables to 0.00145 Mt/year in 2028, then held constant. This is a programme-based aggregate proxy for feed, land, water, farm-expansion and environmental limits; it does not model those resources separately.
model_policy.production_floor: No capture or aquaculture minimum is added. The upper limits do not force production; imports remain the feasibility backstop.
